speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a longstanding pruritic rash and numbness/tingling on your palms; to begin our assessment, do you have a specific occupational exposure to chemicals or solvents, or have you noticed any blisters or scaling on your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT). The clinical triad of blistering/sensitive rash on sun-exposed areas (face/upper body) and neuropathy (numbness/tingling), combined with your occupation involving livestock, strongly suggests this diagnosis, which is often triggered by iron overload or viral hepatitis. Have you noticed any fragility of the skin, such as blisters forming on your fingertips or wrists, or any history of liver disease?
